sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the above, the connection between the eight days of Chanukah and the eight days of Sukkos is explained, as Chanukah also affects the nations, similar to Sukkos.

translations.translation: And based on all the above, the connection of the eight days of Chanukah to the eight days of the festival will also be understood
[as was explained at length in the previous maamar
(beginning with the words "Tanu Rabanan Ner Chanukah"86),
based on the maamarim of our Nesi'im,
that the eight days of Chanukah are analogous to the eight days of the festival]
For just as on Sukkos we cause that "praise87
Hashem, all nations; extol Him, all peoples, for His kindness has overwhelmed us"
[that this "His kindness has overwhelmed us"
(the revelation of the overwhelming of kindness)
also causes the nations and peoples to praise and extol Hashem],
so too is it on Chanukah,
that we also affect the nations and peoples,
as mentioned above
(at the end of section 1 and end of section 7)
regarding the matter of "Kalei Rigla d'Tarmudai," that the light of Ner Chanukah affects even the rebels, that they be in a state of nullification and soul-consumption.
And although on Sukkos the drawing down of "His kindness has overwhelmed us"
(supernal encompassing lights88)
is in complete revelation,
unlike on Chanukah,
for which reason war was then necessary88,
nevertheless, the ruling of the Alter Rebbe89 is known,
that the conclusion of the victory of the war was on the 24th of Kislev,
unlike the 25th of Kislev, which was already a day of rest
[for this is the explanation of Chanukah,
"Chanu Kaf-Heh"90,
that on this day there was rest],
and then "we cleared Your Sanctuary etc. and kindled lights in Your holy courtyards"91,
to the point that there was "to thank and praise Your great Name"91,
which is a very elevated level,
as explained in the discourses of the Exodus from Egypt92
regarding the matter of "His great Name."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as Sukkos is called "the time of our joy" in the plural, reflecting both joys that will be fully realized in the future, so too the effect on the nations during Chanukah, though perfected in the future, is already accomplished now.

translations.translation: Now, just as on Sukkos, "the time of our joy" is in the plural,
referring to the two joys of "Yismach93
Hashem in His works" and "Yismach94
Yisrael in their Maker"95,
even though both are stated in the future tense, because their main essence will be in the future96,
nevertheless, from the fact that the festival of Sukkos is called
(now)
"the time of our joy," it is understood that these two joys also exist now, on Sukkos, in revelation,
so too is it regarding the matter of "Kalei Rigla d'Tarmudai,"
the effect upon the nations during the days of Chanukah,
that although the perfection of this matter will be in the future,
as it is written97
"For then I will turn to the peoples a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of Hashem, to serve Him with one accord,"
nevertheless, this is also done now, on Chanukah98.
And just as it was in those days, that the dominion of the wicked Greek kingdom was nullified,
even though even afterwards there was not yet a complete redemption
[and this is also understood from the fact that in the Second Temple,
both before this and after it,
five things were lacking99],
so too is it in these days, in this time,
that although we are still in the time of exile
(even before the beginning of the redemption100),
nevertheless, through the deeds and service of each and every individual
("for they too were included in that miracle"101)
during the course of the exile,
and particularly in the matter that "time caused it" – the service of the days of Chanukah,
the essence of which is the kindling of the Chanukah lights at the entrance of his house on the outside102,
we bring about "Kalei Rigla d'Tarmudai"
(in both explanations above)
even before the redemption.
And in the manner that it was in the redemption from Egypt
(all exiles are called by the name of Egypt103),
that "for all the Children of Israel there was light in their dwellings" while they were still in Egypt104,
and through this "they emptied out Egypt"105,
like a net that has no grain
(the clarification of the sparks of the revealed world)
and like a deep-sea net that has no fish106
(the clarification of the sparks of the concealed world),
so too is it now,
that in the last moments before the redemption, there will be "for all the Children of Israel light in their dwellings,"
and from this they come afterwards,
and moreover, immediately and at once,
to the complete redemption,
when there will be
(as above)
"Kalei Rigla d'Tarmudai" in its perfection.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Through our deeds and service, especially the study and dissemination of the inner dimension of Torah, we hasten the redemption, leading to the complete redemption with Moshiach.

translations.translation: And 4)
And through our deeds and service, we bring closer and hasten the redemption even more,
as per the ruling of the Rambam85,
that even through a single mitzvah, one causes salvation and deliverance for the entire world,
and certainly through the study and dissemination of the inner dimension of the Torah, which was specifically revealed in the latter generations
(as is known regarding the matter of "those who taste it merit life"107),
and "study is greater, for it leads to action"108,
and this
(the study of the inner dimension of the Torah)
also adds vitality and beauty to the fulfillment of the mitzvos,
to the point of beautification in the manner of "Mehadrin min haMehadrin"
(as is the simple custom regarding the mitzvah of Ner Chanukah109),
and through this we bring closer and hasten the redemption even more,
that very soon we are going to greet Moshiach Tzidkeinu,
who will teach Torah to the entire nation110
(the ultimate perfection in the study of Torah),
and there "we will perform before You as the commandment of Your will"111
(the ultimate perfection in the fulfillment of mitzvos112),
and we will merit "a great congregation that will return here"113,
all of them to thank and praise Your great Name,
in the Third Beis HaMikdash,
the eternal House114,
"the Sanctuary, Hashem, Your hands established"115,
and may it be speedily in our days, literally.
